subject: dental floss
title: What If You Never Flossed?

scenes.text: What if you never flossed? The surprising part: science argued about this for years.
Within hours, a sticky film of bacteria called plaque coats the gaps your brush can't reach.
Leave plaque alone and within days it can harden into tartar, which only a dentist can scrape off.
In a 1965 experiment, volunteers who stopped cleaning their teeth got inflamed gums in 10 to 21 days.
Over years, that can become gum disease. The CDC says 42 percent of American adults over 30 have it.
The twist: in 2016, reporters found the evidence for floss was weak. Cleaning between teeth still beats skipping it.

description:
What if you never flossed? Plaque between teeth can harden into tartar, and in a classic 1965 study gum inflammation appeared within 10 to 21 days without oral hygiene. The CDC says 42% of US adults over 30 have periodontitis.
In 2016 the Associated Press reported the evidence for flossing was weak; a 2019 Cochrane review found floss or interdental brushes with brushing may reduce gum inflammation.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Interdental brushes did slightly better than floss in the 2019 review. Be honest: when did you last floss? And what should we run through next?
